items.title: The tame symbol on a one-dimensional local ring is the norm of the tame symbols of its finite local extensions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section on the tame symbol
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the tame symbol of a pair of nonzerodivisors on a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring as the product of the norms of the tame symbols computed in the finite local extensions B_j, under the hypothesis that the maximal ideal is not an associated prime of B and that B/A is killed by a power of it (statement lines 953-963). The proof first has to make both sides computable: a preparation lemma supplies local extensions C_j in which a and b factor as units times powers of local parameters, and the glueing lemma for maximal ideals assembles them into one finite extension B contained in C, after which both the symbol on A and the symbols on the B_j are written as explicit double and single products of norm terms (proof lines 967-993). The two expressions are then identified by regrouping the product, which is exactly transitivity of the norm in a tower of residue field extensions. The claim is H2: a two-step preparation followed by a norm bookkeeping identity.
